clue.text: Actress, who is no more, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests the words no more are in a sorry, broken state and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A mournful note that a certain actress has died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges NOMORE; 'who is' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Marilyn Monroe was the famous Hollywood film star of the 1950s.

clue.text: Celts, leaving consultancies, organised capital

indicators.note: leaving tells us the letters of the word Celts are taken away from the longer word
organised says the letters that remain are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Celtic staff quit some consultancy firms and set up on their own.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C, E, L, T, S from CONSULTANCIES ('leaving') to get ONUANCIS, then 'organised' rearranges those.
explanation.definitionFit: Asunción is the capital city of Paraguay.

clue.text: Help mistress, partly upset and guileless

indicators.note: upset says the hidden letters are read backwards
partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An innocent servant helping the lady of the house is knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' takes ELPMIS from 'Help mistress'; in a down clue 'upset' turns it upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone guileless is naive and unsophisticated, which is one sense of simple.

clue.text: Sink or swim, for a start, maybe here in Scotland

indicators.note: maybe hints that the letters could be arranged some other way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: for a start points at only the opening letter of the word swim

explanation.surface: A sink-or-swim challenge, perhaps set in some Scottish spot.
explanation.walkthrough: SINKOR plus S, the first letter of 'swim' ('for a start'), make SINKORS, which 'maybe' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinross is a town in Perth and Kinross, a council area of Scotland, so it is a place there.

clue.text: Some Atlantean or Kässbohrer would certainly interest him!

definitions.text: Some Atlantean or Kässbohrer would certainly interest him!

parts.words: Some Atlantean or Kässbohrer would certainly interest him!
parts.note: Atlanteans and Kässbohrers are makes of bus, the kind of vehicle a dedicated spotter would love to log

explanation.surface: Bus spotters love Leyland Atlanteans and Kässbohrer coaches.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter meant a hidden word too, but as printed 'AtlanteAN OR Kässbohrer' is one A short; 'or a Kässbohrer' would have worked. Read it as a description of an obsessive spotter.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang an anorak is an obsessive hobbyist, named for the waterproof jacket trainspotters wear.

clue.text: Coarse Italian patriot, somewhat

indicators.note: somewhat says only part of the patriot's name is wanted, here with its edges trimmed

parts.note: Giuseppe Garibaldi was the patriot who led the unification of Italy

explanation.surface: Describing an Italian national hero as a bit vulgar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' trims GA from the front and I from the back of GARIBALDI.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribald humour is vulgar and earthy, a synonym for coarse.

clue.text: I entirely agree Daisy is wrong accepting French alternative gin's partner

indicators.note: accepting means one piece takes another inside it
is wrong says the letters of Daisy are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

parts.note: ou is French for or, a word offering an alternative
it, short for Italian vermouth, is the partner in gin and it

explanation.surface: Someone insists Daisy is wrong to take some other partner for her gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French alternative' is ou, French for or. Gin and it is a British name for gin with Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom of emphatic agreement: you have said exactly what I think.

clue.text: Juliet's predecessor: one needing first aid, on reflection

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: first takes just the initial letter of the word needing
on reflection says the word aid is mirrored, read from right to left

explanation.surface: Someone in need of first aid after a mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns AID into DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: In the NATO phonetic alphabet the codeword for I comes directly before Juliet, the codeword for J.

clue.text: Delight on large troopship?

definitions.meaning: a big vessel for carrying soldiers or supplies

explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both overwhelming emotion and a ship carrying troops.

clue.text: Wood nymph's uninspiring notice

parts.note: something dry is dull and uninspiring
an ad, short for advertisement, is a public notice

explanation.surface: A forest spirit has put up a dull advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a dryad is a nymph living in trees and woodland.

clue.text: Green cross on Mediterranean island

parts.note: a green light means go
a zo, or dzo, is a cross between a yak and a cow

explanation.surface: An environmentalist annoyed about a Mediterranean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like an environmental adjective; 'on' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gozo is the second-largest island of the Maltese archipelago.

clue.text: Endear fiancee regularly for a Guernsey lily, for example

indicators.note: regularly says to take every other letter of the words, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Win a fiancée's heart by giving her a flower from Guernsey.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the even-numbered letters ('regularly') of 'Endear fiancee'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Guernsey lily belongs to the genus Nerine, flowering bulbs from South Africa.

clue.text: Defensive barrier, square, for rebel holding king

parts.note: to stands in for for, as in the reason for or to

indicators.note: holding means one piece wraps around another

parts.note: Jack Cade led a rebellion in Kent in 1450
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A fortification is put up so a traditionalist can hold off a rebel king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts K inside CADE to make CKADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockade is a wall of upright stakes built for defence, a kind of barrier.

clue.text: Group topped ditch

indicators.note: topped means the head is cut off, losing the first letter

parts.note: ...-ha is a sunken ditch serving as a garden boundary

explanation.surface: A band that has dumped its leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped' removes the first H from HAHA.
explanation.definitionFit: A-ha are the Norwegian pop band behind the hit Take On Me.

clue.text: Old prior, as hermit losing a wee amount

indicators.note: losing means a piece is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: eremite is an old word for a hermit
a mite is a tiny amount

explanation.surface: A former abbot becomes a hermit and loses a little weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old prior' looks like a monastery head; here it is the archaic preposition. 'losing' takes MITE from EREMITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic word for before, so it means prior, as in ere long.

clue.text: Leanest flying kites

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters are tossed about in the air into a new order

explanation.surface: The skinniest kites fly best.
explanation.definitionFit: Elanets are small birds of prey of the kite family.

clue.text: Dusky maiden?

parts.note: the dusky time of day is evening, and the first maiden in Genesis shares that name

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a romantic description of a girl, but points both to twilight and to the first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses at once: the evening and the biblical first woman.

clue.text: Electrical discharge caused by car crash

indicators.note: caused by says the answer is produced by, and found within, the words that follow

explanation.surface: An electrical spark after a car collision.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'cAR Crash'; it looks like an anagram of car, which also works, but the setter hid it.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc is a luminous electrical discharge across a gap between electrodes.

clue.text: Young Treherne appearing regularly

indicators.note: appearing regularly says to take letters at regular intervals, the first, third and so on

explanation.surface: A young person named Treherne turns up often.
explanation.definitionFit: Teen is used adjectivally for adolescent, a synonym for young.

clue.text: Doc embraces member backing eastern chum

indicators.note: backing says the combined piece is read in reverse
embraces means the word wraps its arms round another

parts.note: the word doc, taken as written
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A doctor hugs a club member who supports his eastern friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' gives DARMOC, and 'backing' turns it into COMRAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A comrade is a companion or mate, a synonym of chum.

clue.text: Customers who have taken vows?

definitions.meaning: frequent patrons of a pub or shop
monks and nuns bound by a religious rule, the regular clergy

explanation.walkthrough: The regular clergy live under a religious rule, unlike secular priests; the question mark flags this less familiar sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means habitual patrons and also members of religious orders.

clue.text: Means to close entrance to labyrinth?

definitions.text: Means to close entrance to labyrinth?

parts.words: Means to close entrance to labyrinth?
parts.note: the labyrinth is also the inner ear, whose entrance can be blocked by a small stopper

explanation.walkthrough: It suggests a gate for the Minotaur's maze, but the labyrinth is the inner ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug of foam or wax that blocks the ear canal against noise.

clue.text: Greek character touring Crete, swimming and so forth

indicators.note: touring means going round, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: swimming says the letters of Crete move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A Greek holidaymaker tours Crete, swims, and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' wants to be a person on holiday; it is just a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Et cetera is Latin for and the rest, used to mean and so on.

clue.text: Display and make lace as well

parts.note: to tat is to make tatting, a knotted lace
too means also, as well

explanation.surface: Show off your work and do some lacemaking too.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is a military display, such as the Edinburgh Military Tattoo.

clue.text: Decadent English/French social function

parts.note: a fête is a festive gathering or celebration

explanation.surface: A decadent party where the English and French mingle.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete describes something weak and self-indulgent, close to decadent.

clue.text: Initially, Alan the entrepreneur returns to Mediterranean island city

indicators.note: returns says the pieces are read back to front
initially takes the first letter of the name Alan

parts.note: Alan Sugar is a British business magnate of TV's The Apprentice

explanation.surface: Alan Sugar goes back to a Sicilian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reverses A SUGAR. Lord Sugar is a well-known British businessman and TV presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragusa is a city on Sicily, the Mediterranean island (and the old name of Dubrovnik).

clue.text: Its partition was booked

parts.note: a body of water whose parting by Moses is recorded in a book of the Bible, Exodus

explanation.walkthrough: 'booked' sounds like a reservation, but means written down in a book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: In Exodus Moses parts this sea so the Israelites can cross.

clue.text: Shelter for fine candlestick

definitions.meaning: a small fort or earthwork protecting a position
at Oxford colleges, a penalty of drinking a large quantity of ale
a candle holder fixed to a wall

explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings with 'for' as the link: a small fort, an Oxford forfeit, and a wall bracket for candles.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word covers a fortification, an Oxford forfeit and a wall-mounted light holder.

clue.text: Teachers' pole

definitions.meaning: the employees of a school taken together
a stick or rod, as in a walking stick

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a body of employees and a long stick.

clue.text: Veteran officer in charge keeps unusual dope for local medication

indicators.note: keeps means one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: veteran means old

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of dope are set out in an odd order

parts.note: OC is the military abbreviation for officer commanding or in charge

explanation.surface: An old commanding officer is caught with some odd drugs for a home remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' means applied to one spot, as in local anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Opodeldoc was a soap-based liniment rubbed onto sore spots, a topical remedy.

clue.text: River abroad

definitions.meaning: a Scottish river flowing into the Firth past Edinburgh
out and away, as in went out into the world

explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' here means out of doors or out into the world, not overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish river, and an old adverb meaning outwards, away.

clue.text: Price rush organised for millionaires' class

indicators.note: organised says the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Prices rise in a rush, arranged for the wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: The very wealthiest people, a social class above mere millionaires.
